breaks.expected: A row the database ACCEPTED and committed must be deliverable (sign with iat clamped/tolerated for small skew, or read the isolate clock before the RPC and refuse BEFORE spending), so a generation is never spent for a response the client never receives. Free-path callers recover on retry (tickets are re-issued), Pro callers burn a generation per retry while the skew persists; every retry lands 503 again if skew >= 1 s persists, so the route is effectively down for that deployment pair while nothing is 'unavailable'.
breaks.observed: VERIFIED: the RPC is called exactly once (generation 1 committed on the DB side), then the route answers 503 {"error":{"message":"Offline grant issuance is temporarily unavailable. Root cause (VERIFIED by code read): signOfflineExecutionGrant() -> validateBoundClaims() throws OfflineGrantCryptoError('invalid_time') when context.nowEpochSeconds < claims.iat; index.ts only computes nowEpochSeconds AFTER the RPC returned, so a DB-committed row can never be delivered when floor(db now()) > floor(isolate Date.now()). No skew tolerance exists on the issuance side.
